text:
Predicates:
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
MountainRange(x) ::: x is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Mine(x) ::: x is a mine.
Donated(x) ::: x was donated.
In(x, y) ::: x is in y.
InTexas(x) ::: x is in Texas.
InNewMexico(x) ::: x is in New Mexico.
HasMine(x) ::: x has a mine.
HaveBeenDonated(x) ::: x has been donated.
Question:  
JuanDeOnateVisitedMountainRangeInNewMexico ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in New Mexico.

Premises:  
MountainRange(picurisMountains) ∧ LocatedIn(picurisMountains, NewMexico) ::: The Picuris Mountains are in New Mexico or Texas.  
Visited(JuanDeOnate, picurisMountains) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.  
∃x (Mine(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, picurisMountains) ∧ Donated(x)) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine, located in the Picuris Mountains, was donated.  
∀x ((MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, Texas) ∧ ∃y (Mine(y) ∧ LocatedIn(y, x) ∧ Donated(y))) → ⊥) ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas with donated mines.  

Conclusion:  
JuanDeOnateVisitedMountainRangeInNewMexico ::: ∃x (MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, NewMexico) ∧ Visited(JuanDeOnate, x))
